page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.32xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using KVM hypervisor technology. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system includes 256.0 GB of memory, allocating 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. This 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio aligns with resource requirements for compute-bound processing tasks.

The instance operates without bundled local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring attached network storage solutions for persistent data needs. Network throughput is supported by a baseline network bandwidth of 64 Gbps, facilitating rapid data transfers across cloud infrastructure. It does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From a resource density perspective, the high vCPU core count combined with substantial network throughput offers cost efficiency for large-scale compute workloads that do not demand extensive local storage or high memory-per-core ratios. The primary tradeoff is the total reliance on remote storage volumes for system and application data. Workload fits include high-performance compute clusters, batch processing, application servers, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and web serving clusters requiring intensive parallel CPU execution.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.32xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is equipped with 128 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.7 GHz, paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance lacks bundled local disk storage and integrated GPU acceleration, relying on external network storage for disk operations. Network performance is backed by a 64 Gbps baseline bandwidth, providing high data transmission capability across cloud infrastructure. Without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, network accessibility requires configured routing or elastic IPs. The high core density and dedicated CPU allocation offer strong resource efficiency for CPU-heavy tasks without paying for unused local storage. Suitable workloads include intensive parallel compute jobs, batch processing systems, application backend fleets, compilation servers, and large-scale web microservices.
